caption: The day-1 iron farm: for 11 iron (the shears for its leaves counted) and no quartz, three villagers scared by a zombie summon iron golems that burn in lava pits, about 295 iron an hour (62% of the game's ceiling). Three villagers sleep on their beds in closed 1-cell pods under leaves; a zombie in a boat 7 blocks north is in view of their standing and sleeping eyes. Golems spawn in a row of 8 1x1 pits west of the zombie, a lava source beside their head on both sides, and burn where they stand. One tripwire runs through every pit at knee height: a golem in any pit opens the trapdoor in front of the zombie, which hides it, and the villagers calm down (at night they fall asleep) while the golem burns. A water channel under the string carries the iron to one hopper. Hide the zombie by hand on the first night: the villagers need a recent sleep to summon the first golem. Game check (the real 26.3 server, this layout): 8 runs of 6 days, 72.8 golems/h (95% of the mean 70.3-75.3) against redsim's 74.8; 579 golems by day and 586 by night; spawn cells chi-square 6.25 over 8 cells (5% critical value 14.0).

The middle iron farm: for 18 iron (the tools counted) and 6 quartz, four villagers summon a golem every 32 seconds, 443 iron an hour (93% of the game's ceiling), each golem dropping out of their sight at once. Four villagers sleep on beds in closed 1-cell pods under leaves (only three must agree, so a golem one of them sees does not stretch the cycle); a zombie in a boat 7 blocks north is in their view. At nightfall two inverted daylight detectors open the three trapdoors in front of the zombie for 46 game ticks: the villagers fall asleep, then wake up scared for the rest of the night (the farm restarts by itself after a missed night). Golems spawn on a 6x6 pad; water from its corners pushes them onto the hole's ring (water over open fence gates: it holds the water, not a golem) and into its dry 2x2 center (open fence gates stop the water), and they fall 16 blocks out of every villager's sight to water that pushes them under a lava blade held by fence gates, a ceiling right above it, over two hoppers. Game check (the real 26.3 server, this file): 8 runs of 3 days, 114.5 golems/h (95% of the mean 113.1-115.9) against redsim's 112.3 (redsim reads 2% low); 451 golems by day and 465 by night; spawn cells chi-square 15.89 over 20 cells (5% critical value 30.1).

The fastest iron farm module: 459 iron an hour (96% of the game's ceiling) for 18 iron (the tools counted) and 6 quartz; build copies 27 blocks apart to scale it (iron-scaled-2x2: 4 copies, 1836 iron an hour). Four villagers sleep on beds in closed 1-cell pods under leaves (only three must agree, so a golem one of them sees does not stretch the cycle); a zombie in a boat 7 blocks north is in their view. At nightfall two inverted daylight detectors open the three trapdoors in front of the zombie for 46 game ticks: the villagers fall asleep, then wake up scared for the rest of the night (the farm restarts by itself after a missed night). Golems spawn on an 8x8 pad; water from its corners pushes them onto the hole's ring (water over open fence gates: it holds the water, not a golem) and into its dry 2x2 center (open fence gates stop the water), and they fall 16 blocks out of every villager's sight to water that pushes them under a lava blade held by fence gates, a ceiling right above it, over two hoppers. Game check (the real 26.3 server, this layout): 8 runs of 3 days, 116.0 golems/h (95% of the mean 112.3-119.7) against redsim's 115.2; 461 golems by day and 467 by night; spawn cells chi-square 49.30 over 48 cells (5% critical value 64.0).

The fastest iron farm, scaled: four copies of the fastest module 27 blocks apart make 1836 iron an hour (96% of four modules' ceiling) for 48 iron (the tools counted) and 24 quartz. Each module: four villagers sleep on beds in closed 1-cell pods under leaves (only three must agree); a zombie in a boat 7 blocks north is in their view; at nightfall two inverted daylight detectors open the three trapdoors in front of the zombie for 46 game ticks, so the villagers sleep once and wake up scared. Golems spawn on an 8x8 pad, water pushes them over a ring of water held by open fence gates into a dry 2x2 center, and they fall 16 blocks out of sight to water that pushes them under a lava blade, over two hoppers. At 27 blocks no golem of one module is ever in another module's villagers' follow range. One chest per module. Game check (the real 26.3 server, this layout): 2 runs of 3 days, 462 golems/h (95% of the mean 438.5-485.5) against redsim's 461.2; 462 golems by day and 462 by night; spawn cells chi-square 210.89 over 192 cells (5% critical value 224.2).

The obvious iron farm (the bar to beat): villagers scared by a zombie by day, asleep by night, summon golems that water carries to a lava blade, 139 iron an hour (29% of the game's ceiling). Three villagers sleep on their beds in closed 1-cell pods under leaves; a zombie in a boat 7 blocks north is in their view. An inverted daylight detector opens the trapdoor in front of the zombie at nightfall, so the villagers sleep through every night (and the farm restarts by itself after a missed night); it stops in rain (clear weather is not judged). Golems spawn on a 6x5 pad 4 below the villagers; water from its far edge carries them into a trench along its near edge (wall signs hold the water over it; open fence gates hold the pad's water at its sides); they fall to water that pushes them under a lava blade held by signs, a ceiling right above it, over two hoppers. Every golem stays in the villagers' sight until it dies, which is what the other farms avoid. Game check (the real 26.3 server, this file): 8 runs of 3 days, 35.0 golems/h (95% of the mean 34.1-35.9) against redsim's 35.7; 278 golems by day and 2 by night; spawn cells chi-square 22.42 over 20 cells (5% critical value 30.1).
